Denote S n the set of permutations in [ n ] and µ = µ n the uniform distribution on S n . In addition, denote by ν = ν n the uniform distribution on {-1 , +1 } n . We will use the following notation conventions for graphs.

- Labeled graphs . Denote by K n the complete graph with vertex set [ n ] and edge set U n . For any graph H , let V ( H ) denote the vertex set of H and let E ( H ) denote the edge set of H . We say H is a subgraph of G , denoted by H ⊂ G , if V ( H ) ⊂ V ( G ) and E ( H ) ⊂ E ( G ). We say φ : V ( H ) → V ( S ) is an injection, if for all ( i, j ) ∈ E ( H ) we have ( φ ( i ) , φ ( j )) ∈ E ( S ). For H,S ⊂ K n , denote by H ∩ S the graph with vertex set given by V ( H ) ∩ V ( S ) and edge set given by E ( H ) ∩ E ( S ), and denote by S ∪ H the graph with vertex set given by V ( H ) ∪ V ( S ) and edge set given by E ( H ) ∪ E ( S ). For any graph H , denote the excess of H by τ ( H ) = | E ( H ) | - | V ( H ) | . Given u ∈ V ( H ), define Nei H ( u ) to be the set of neighbors of u in H . For two vertices u, v ∈ V ( H ), we define Dist H ( u, v ) to be their graph distance. Denote the diameter of a connected graph H by Diam ( H ) = max u,v ∈ V ( H ) Dist H ( u, v ).
- Graph isomorphisms and unlabeled graphs. Two graphs H and H ′ are isomorphic, denoted by H ∼ = H ′ , if there exists a bijection π : V ( H ) → V ( H ′ ) such that ( π ( u ) , π ( v )) ∈ E ( H ′ ) if and only if ( u, v ) ∈ E ( H ). Denote by H the isomorphism class of graphs; it is customary to refer to these isomorphic classes as unlabeled graphs. Let Aut( H ) be the number of automorphisms of H (graph isomorphisms to itself). For any graph H , define Fix ( H ) = { u ∈ V ( H ) : φ ( u ) = u, ∀ φ ∈ Aut( H ) } .
- Induced subgraphs . For a graph H = ( V, E ) and a subset A ⊂ V , define H A = ( A,E A ) to be the induced subgraph of H in A , where E A = { ( u, v ) ∈ E : u, v ∈ A } . Also, define H \ A = ( V, E \ A ) to be the subgraph of H obtained by deleting all edges with both endpoints in A . Note that E A ∪ E \ A = E .
- Isolated vertices . For u ∈ V ( H ), we say u is an isolated vertex of H if there is no edge in E ( H ) incident to u . Denote I ( H ) as the set of isolated vertices of H .

- Paths, self-avoiding paths and non-backtracking paths. We say a subgraph H ⊂ K n is a path with endpoints u, v (possibly with u = v ), if there exist w 1 , . . . , w m ∈ [ n ] = u, v such that V ( H ) = { u, v, w 1 , . . . , w m } and E ( H ) = { ( u, w 1 ) , ( w 1 , w 2 ) . . . , ( w m , v ) } (we allow the occurrence of multiple vertices or edges). We say H is a self-avoiding path if w 0 , w 1 , . . . , w m , w m +1 are distinct (where we denote w 0 = u and w m +1 = v ), and we say H is a non-backtracking path if w i +1 = w i -1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ m . Denote EndP( P ) as the set of endpoints of a path P .

- Cycles and independent cycles. We say a subgraph H is an m -cycle if V ( H ) = { v 1 , . . . , v m } and E ( H ) = { ( v 1 , v 2 ) , . . . , ( v m -1 , v m ) , ( v m , v 1 ) } . For a subgraph K ⊂ H , we say K is an independent m -cycle of H , if K is an m -cycle and no edge in E ( H ) \ E ( K ) is incident to V ( K ). Denote C m ( H ) as the set of independent m -cycles of H . For H ⊂ S , we define C m ( S, H ) to be the set of independent m -cycles in S whose vertex set is disjoint from V ( H ).
- Leaves. A vertex u ∈ V ( H ) is called a leaf of H , if the degree of u in H is 1; denote L ( H ) as the set of leaves of H .
- Trees and rooted trees . We say a graph T = ( V ( T ) , E ( T )) is a tree, if T is connected and has no cycles.
